description: Start a job that turns 360 footage into a Gaussian splat scene you can walk through. Input is one public https URL (source_url) or several (source_urls) and the kind: equirect_video (a stitched 2:1 equirectangular video from any 360 camera), equirect_images (a set of stitched 360 photos) or insv (raw Insta360 video; pass both files of a split pair in source_urls). A single 360 photo, raw .insp included, has no camera movement to build a splat from: use pano_scene_create for it. MCP clients cannot stream multi-gigabyte files, so the file must already be at a public https URL; for a file on disk use the CLI, which uploads it in parts: `npx three-ws capture 360 <file>`. Optional trim ({start_s, end_s}) limits a long video and quality is preview, standard (default) or high. Returns a job_id at once; the job runs on a GPU and takes minutes to over an hour (conservatively 10 to 25 minutes for preview, 25 to 60 for standard, 60 to 120 for high, plus a few minutes of GPU start-up when idle). Collect it with pano_capture_status. The result is owned files: a PLY and an SPZ splat, a flythrough preview video, a poster image and a viewer link. Use this when the user has 360 camera footage and wants a 3D scene from it. Needs a free three.ws account.

quality.description: preview is fastest, standard is the default, high uses more frames and training and takes longest.

source_kind.description: What the URL points at: equirect_video, equirect_images or insv.

source_url.description: Public https URL of one file: a stitched 360 video or one raw .insv.

source_urls.description: Public https URLs of a split pair of .insv files (both lenses), or of a set of equirect photos.

trim.description: Use only part of a video.

start_s.description: Seconds to skip at the start.

name: pano_capture_start
title: Turn 360 footage into a Gaussian splat
